title: LLM Engineering and Fine-Tuning
summary: Build, adapt and evaluate large language models. You will fine-tune an open-weight model on your own dataset, connect it to retrieval pipelines and measure whether it actually improved.
outcomes: Fine-tune an open-weight model with LoRA and QLoRA
Design a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline with a vector index
Evaluate model quality with repeatable benchmarks instead of impressions
Serve a quantized model behind a documented API

title: Applied Machine Learning Foundations
summary: The required foundation for the advanced AI track. Learn to prepare data, train supervised models and judge results honestly before moving on to neural networks and language models.
outcomes: Prepare and validate a tabular dataset in Python
Train, tune and compare classical machine learning models
Explain the main sources of overfitting and how to detect them
Build and train a small neural network from scratch

title: AI Security and Red Teaming
summary: Test language model applications the way an attacker would. Cover prompt injection, data leakage and unsafe tool use, then design the controls that stop them.
outcomes: Identify prompt injection and jailbreak paths in an LLM application
Threat-model an application that uses retrieval and tools
Build an automated red-team test suite with clear pass and fail criteria
Recommend layered controls and document the residual risk

modules.title: Defenses and Guardrails
modules.topics: Input and output filtering, least privilege, monitoring

title: Penetration Testing Professional
summary: A complete penetration testing course, from reconnaissance to a professional report. Every technique is practiced in isolated lab networks, under written rules of engagement.
outcomes: Run a full penetration test methodology from scoping to reporting
Enumerate and exploit weaknesses in network and Active Directory environments
Escalate privileges and document attack paths clearly
Write a report that a technical team can act on and an executive can read

title: Web Application Security
summary: Find and fix the flaws that cause most real-world breaches in web applications and APIs. You will test vulnerable applications, then write the secure code that closes the gaps.
outcomes: Find injection, cross-site scripting and access control flaws in web applications
Test REST and GraphQL APIs for authorization and data exposure issues
Review application code for secure coding defects
Explain each finding with a proof of concept and a tested fix

title: Security Operations and Threat Hunting
summary: Learn how a Security Operations Center detects and triages threats. Write detection rules, hunt for attackers who evade alerts and map what you find to MITRE ATT&CK.
outcomes: Collect, normalize and search security logs in a SIEM
Write and tune detection rules, including Sigma rules
Triage alerts and decide quickly between noise and incident
Run a threat hunt from a hypothesis to a documented finding

title: Digital Forensics and Incident Response
summary: Investigate a compromised system from start to finish. Preserve evidence correctly, reconstruct what happened and produce findings that stand up to scrutiny.
outcomes: Acquire and preserve digital evidence with a documented chain of custody
Analyze disk images, memory captures and artifacts for attacker activity
Build a timeline of an intrusion from multiple sources
Write an incident report and a lessons-learned review
